seo_description: Plano kids' Christmas: Santa photos at Legacy West, Holiday Lights at Assembly Park, Gift of Christmas, Nutcracker, Scrooge and the Interurban museum.
lede: The story of Christmas in Plano starts with a railroad town that the Houston and Texas Central line reached in 1872 and an interurban station that opened on July 1, 1908, and today it runs from Historic Downtown Plano, where Dickens in Downtown Plano lights the Arts District each year, to the North Pole at Legacy West and the Gift of Christmas stage show at Prestonwood Baptist Church. Plano's 2026 season counts 35 events on this page, from free ornament painting at McCall Plaza to the Holiday Lights at Assembly Park.
sections: A town named for a plain, on the railroad since 1872

Settlers reached southwestern Collin County in the 1840s, and postal authorities approved the name Plano in 1852. Dr. Henry Dye suggested it from a Spanish word he understood to mean plain, a nod to the flat land around town. The Houston and Texas Central Railway connected the community to Dallas in 1872, and Plano was platted and incorporated in 1873. A fire in 1881 destroyed 52 buildings and left the town a tent city for a while. Plano had 1,304 people in 1900 and 222,030 in 2000, and by the mid 1980s it had overtaken McKinney as the commercial center of Collin County.
The Interurban depot that became a museum

Plano's Christmas has a railroad heart. The Texas Traction Company was chartered on September 25, 1906, the first interurban trip ran on June 30, 1908, and Plano's station opened for business on July 1, 1908. After a 1917 merger it became the Texas Electric Railway, with more than 200 miles of track. The depot burned in the late 1920s and was rebuilt smaller, and passenger service ended in 1948. The City of Plano renovated the station in 1990 and opened it as the Interurban Railway Museum, run with the Plano Conservancy, where Texas Electric Railway Passenger Motor 360 still sits beside the depot.
Downtown, Dickens and the new North Pole

Downtown Plano's biggest night is Dickens in Downtown Plano, a free annual celebration in the Downtown Plano Arts District with photos with Santa, a snow slide, a Coffee and Cocoa Walk, a Children's Entrepreneur Market and a tree lighting with the mayor in Haggard Park, McCall Plaza and on 15th Street. In 2026, free Santa pictures at Willis Morrison State Farm on December 12 and a free Ornament Paint Night at McCall Plaza on December 18 also fall in the district. Across town, Legacy West runs a North Pole with Santa photos on December 4 to 6, 11 and 12, and Assembly Park lights its playground every evening.
trains: The DART light rail system serves Richardson and Plano, and its Red Line ends at Parker Road Station in Plano, which makes a car-free trip from Dallas possible for families. The big train story in Plano itself is the 1908 interurban station, now the Interurban Railway Museum, built for the Texas Electric Railway that ran from 1908 to 1948. Within reach are the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley in Dallas and the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco.

faq: How did Plano get its name?

Postal authorities approved the name Plano in 1852. Dr. Henry Dye suggested it from a Spanish word he understood to mean plain, because the land around the settlement was flat. The Houston and Texas Central Railway reached the town in 1872, and Plano was platted and incorporated in 1873, according to the Handbook of Texas.
When did the interurban train come to Plano?

Plano's interurban station opened for business on July 1, 1908, after the first interurban trip on June 30. The Texas Electric Railway ran through town until passenger service ended in 1948. The City of Plano renovated the old station in 1990, and it is now the Interurban Railway Museum, which families can visit with kids.
What is Dickens in Downtown Plano?

Dickens in Downtown Plano is a free annual celebration in the Downtown Plano Arts District. The 2024 edition, held on December 7, had photos with Santa, a snow slide, the Coffee and Cocoa Walk, the Children's Entrepreneur Market and a tree lighting with the mayor, in Haggard Park, McCall Plaza and on 15th Street.
Where can kids meet Santa in Plano in 2026?

Willis Morrison State Farm, 1027 E 15th Street, offers free pictures with Santa on December 12, from 3 to 6 pm, with an online RSVP. Legacy West runs Santa photos on December 4 to 6, 11 and 12, from 11 am to 3 pm, at $36.64 per photo session.
Are there free Christmas lights in Plano?

Yes. Holiday Lights at Assembly Park, 6200 K Avenue in east Plano, turns the park playground into a glowing display every evening from 4 to 11 pm through January 6, 2027. The Visit Plano events calendar lists it as free, with no tickets or set times, so families can stroll and take photos.
Can we ride a train to Plano?

DART light rail serves Plano, and the Red Line ends at Parker Road Station in Plano. For a train outing in town, the Interurban Railway Museum sits in the 1908 interurban station. Check the museum's hours before you go, and check each event's page for parking if you plan to drive.
